payload.entry: Planning investigation on clean sase 9066546900ccafffcd3846f1ff56b81580c1f515, athena, Python 3.14.7, opened sase-core e60f3e1658d34f1345bc4bef8bf112a396749c87. Both prior fixes are present. Original bounded-render node passed isolated (1.30s call). Deterministic fault injection created a fresh owner-free sidecar .git/index.lock immediately before the existing blocked renderer, using an in-memory pytest plugin and dataclasses.replace on PublicationTransactionHooks; no product/test files changed. Original assertion then failed at elapsed=15.6448s: render entered 0.155s after transaction start and unwound at 0.830s with alarm=True; locked drain duration=15.625s, cleanup=14.6253s, first alarm stage=hood_publish:foo. Git logged six backoffs (0.1..3.2s), then a 7.666s stale-age wait and lock removal. The one-shot alarm is spent before exception cleanup. agents_sync.git.run_git supplies neither a remaining deadline to run_with_git_lock_retry nor a reduced subprocess timeout. Core git_lock::maybe_backoff also ignores remaining deadline/budget fields (age-wait consults them). This proves a concrete post-alarm failure mode, not a spontaneous reproduction of the historical loaded lane. Preparing a medium tale for bounded cleanup, Rust deadline-policy enforcement, and integration regressions; work remains unimplemented pending the requested plan handoff.

PLANNING EVIDENCE: At clean sase HEAD 9066546900, _ArtifactFileCache.select_prompt_file still admits raw_prompt.md and sorts only by descending st_mtime_ns. A mocked-filesystem probe of the real method selects raw at equal mtimes with raw-first enumeration, selects expanded when enumeration reverses, and selects raw again when its mtime is newer. This confirms a product precedence defect; apollo candidate timestamps/order still need measuring before asserting the exact host trigger. The four primary files pass on athena (Python 3.14.7, pytest -q -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider): 30 passed in 4.54s. No implementation changes made. Authored and validated a medium tale for Rust-owned selection policy, Python cache integration, deterministic tie/raw-exclusion regressions, and cross-host verification. No epic-symbol entries currently reference this phase.

TASK RESOLVED: sase-15h — evidence: base sase-core e60f3e16 on athena. Mechanism confirmed live two ways: (1) new deterministic test holds a script open for writing across a forked sleep child and the exec fails with ETXTBSY os error 26; (2) a parallel-suite run produced a live ETXTBSY on a script whose writer had already closed (foreign inheritor) — the exact fleet flake shape. Fix: publish_executable (write-tmp + chmod + atomic rename under a process-wide spawn lock) for every sudo_runner script writer — Fixture::new fake-sudo/fake-executor, write_executable (waiting-worker + 6 worker.rs sites), 2 direct worker.rs writes converted to the helper; per-spawn-attempt lock inside retry_on_etxtbsy (cfg(test)-only, never across waits/sleeps); bounded ETXTBSY-only retry (250x2ms) at all 5 spawn sites as documented backstop. No assertion changed; dispatch relative.txt + manifest/marker JSON are never execd data files, intentionally unchanged.

Verification: 56/56 sudo_runner tests pass (53 existing + 3 new etxtbsy regression tests); 15/15 parallel stress iterations green; sase tool run check in sase-core verdict pass (run 570abe2c0c68d1cc1d33a5c51c31a32b). Limits: an intermediate whole-run lock design broke 2 timing tests (75ms stop-file, 2s live-log poll) and was replaced with per-spawn-attempt guards — both pass since. No memory edits per keep_five_seeds. No wire/binding changes, so no sase-core pin move is needed from this phase. sase-core tree left uncommitted for host finalizers (agents never commit). No PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: adjacent sase-15e/sase-15f are separately owned beads, untouched.

sudo_runner ETXTBSY fixture race fixed in sase-core: atomic script publication under a spawn lock + per-spawn guards + bounded ETXTBSY retry backstop at all 5 spawn sites; every assertion kept. Verified: 56/56 focused pass, 15/15 stress iterations green, sase tool run check verdict pass (570abe2c). No epic-symbol leftovers.

Integration reviewed a79207993c staged-handoff reclaim, b8145cb51a clan navigation, 82cf081fc4 publication observation split; no unrelated core drift after e60f3e16 and current pin contains all phase commits. REMAINING EPIC WORK: cleanup optional-binding/Python-1.0 fallback violates required Rust boundary (missing-binding probe returns 1.0; explicit Python override ignores a smaller mocked Rust cap); core handoff.rs has two retry_on_etxtbsy(command.status) calls holding the cfg(test) fixture lock through child wait; ETXTBSY inheritance test retains the writer in the parent and retry test depends on sleep scheduling; startup footprint integration is over budget as recorded in FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE. Plan a single medium tale to repair these and perform full closeout, with no dependency on its own commit or CI. No epic-symbol entries; no parent_bead (predecessor plan link is not a parent). LANDING REPAIRS (tale 202611/finish_1qt_landing.md, same-turn closeout; host commits and the sase-core pin follow this note, so no SHA is cited for them). Audited tips unchanged at closeout: sase d26baecb05 == origin/master, sase-core 45c6a260 == origin/master; no drift to reconcile.

1. REQUIRED RUST CLEANUP POLICY. default_publication_cleanup_timeout now goes through require_rust_binding in the core adapter; the optional-binding path and both Python 1.0 mirrors are gone. A missing/stale/raising binding raises (adapter and PublicationCleanupBudget alike); non-numeric, non-positive or non-finite values raise RuntimeError. An override can only shorten the Rust-owned cap (min); a non-positive override raises ValueError. _commit_publication_locked builds the budget inside the protected cleanup boundary, so a lookup failure is attached as a note to the original exception (drain timeout stays primary, request stays queued with attempts==1, sidecar lock released) and no cleanup runs with an invented default. The shared one-second cap and the elapsed<5s assertions are untouched. sase-core: dropped the core_default_publication_cleanup_timeout alias from sase_core_py prelude.rs; vcs/mod.rs uses the module path. No binding contract change, so no pin move is owed. New tests/agents_sync/test_publication_cleanup_policy.py (17 tests: missing, raising, malformed values, override-cannot-exceed-cap, original-exception and timeout-attribution preservation, a 0.25s Rust cap bounding a stalled cleanup).

2. SUDO FIXTURE LOCK SCOPE (sase-core). retry_on_etxtbsy is now typed as a spawn (FnMut -> io::Result<Child>): the cfg(test) fixture spawn lock covers one Command::spawn attempt and is released before any wait or backoff; a spawn that returned Ok is never retried; only ETXTBSY is retried. New status_with_etxtbsy_retry spawns under the guard and waits outside it; handoff.rs sudo_status and spawn_internal_root_executor use it (the two sites that held the lock through the child wait). Test-only output_with_etxtbsy_retry replaces the .output() closures. DETERMINISTIC EVIDENCE: tests/spawn_lock.rs keeps a real sudo child alive on a handshake file and proves another fixture publication plus spawn completes meanwhile (bounded recv_timeout, self-expiring child, drop-guard release); mutation check holding the lock through the wait made both tests fail (and cascaded into internal_worker_timeout_completes_when_descendant_holds_pipe), then reverted. etxtbsy.rs: the exec_while_fork_child test now has a real child hold the inherited non-CLOEXEC writer, confirms it via a ready marker, closes the parent's copy, asserts ETXTBSY, releases and reaps the child, then proves exec succeeds; the retry test closes the writer inside the retry loop only after observing the first failed attempt (no sleeps or threads) and still asserts a retry happened. Bare result.is_ok() assertions in sudo_runner cli.rs/worker.rs now print the Err (9 sites). Every executable writer still goes through publish_executable/write_executable; manifest/argv/marker data stay data.

3. STARTUP FOOTPRINT. Edges deferred: sase.agents_sync package __init__ is now a PEP 562 lazy facade (via sase._lazy_exports), ACE agents_sync action imports sync_agents at its use site, artifact-link stitch rules import agents_sync.git.run_git at use, commit_finalizer_git_progress imports AGENTS_SYNC_AUTO_COMMIT_TYPE at use. The deferred-module guard gained agents_sync.git, git_sync, git_sync_transaction, publication, publication_cleanup; allowances, CPU bound and total-module guard unchanged. Normalized source footprint: base 9066546900 = 12,161,158 (2860 modules); d26baecb05 = 12,166,370; strict cap 12,162,484; now 11,893,483 bytes, 2796 sase.* modules (3506 total), i.e. -272,887 vs d26baecb05, -267,675 vs base, 269,001 under the cap. Attributed report (tools/tui_import_closure --diff d26baecb05): @attachment:closure_final_vs_head.txt

VERIFICATION. sase: sase tool run check c3d751031ae96ebbfdca08ab1cfe32bc succeeded (38m). sase-core: sase tool run check 141fcdc410d4549d8645dce189f6a0ab succeeded (646s). sudo_runner module 58 passed, then 60/60 repeated runs (12 concurrent processes x 5 rounds, 24 busy loops). Bounded-drain + policy modules 26 passed, 12/12 concurrent loaded runs (16 busy loops; young-lock cleanup case 2.43-2.50s, stalled-cleanup case 2.06-2.08s vs the 5s bound). Prompt cache/render, git-lock, import-budget and closure files: 231 passed. Wider sweeps: agents_sync+artifact_links+core recovery 752 passed; every test file mentioning agents_sync plus llm_provider and sdd 2362 passed, 1 failed (see limits).
